items.review_rationale: Read scheme Zariski topology on the underlying locally ringed space, with its consistency on affine Spec charts, their prime-spectrum topology and principal distinguished opens.

references.phrase: scheme X with underlying locally ringed space

references.context: Principal Zariski open of primes not containing f, forming a basis of the affine chart.
Restriction of scheme topology to an affine open is the corresponding prime-spectrum Zariski topology.

references.phrase: locally characterized by all affine charts
references.disposition: Topology compatibility on charts is used to characterize scheme topology; this is not the constructible or étale topology.

items.review_rationale: Read adjacency matrix construction for a finite simple undirected graph, including chosen vertex enumeration, indicator entries and absence of loops; noted dependence on ordering.

references.context: A bijective enumeration of graph vertices by 1 through n, required to index matrix rows and columns.
Square array indexed by ordered vertices with binary indicator entries.
Entry equals 1 precisely when unordered pair {v_i,v_j} is an edge; otherwise 0.

references.phrase: simple undirected implies zero diagonal and symmetric matrix
references.disposition: These follow from looplessness and unordered edges and are not further data.

items.review_rationale: Read two-part partition of vertices with every edge crossing between disjoint parts, and kept potential empty parts distinct from mandatory nonempty bipartitions.

references.phrase: bipartite graph variant in same corpus
crossing edge between A and B
references.context: Each unordered graph edge has one endpoint in A and the other in B.

references.phrase: A and B may be empty
references.disposition: The stated condition does not demand both parts be nonempty; for edge-free graphs an empty part is allowed.

items.review_rationale: Read a Boolean ring in the possibly nonunital associative-ring convention with universal idempotence, and preserved its difference from the unital ring convention without assuming an identity.

references.context: Additive abelian group and associative distributive multiplication; existence of multiplicative identity is not assumed.
Every ring element multiplied by itself equals itself, the defining Boolean property.

references.disposition: The absence of an assumed unity is material; do not equate its scope with the unital Boolean-ring variant.
